subject: ClarionHealth: probe gaps during maintenance window / request for ledger breakdown
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@clarionhealth.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-19T18:41:00Z
Subject: Re: Production errors during maintenance — ledger mismatch

Hi Sergio,

We spotted an availability blip in our dashboards during your scheduled maintenance window last night and our finance/org team is asking for a ledger breakdown. Quick summary: between 02:15-02:30 UTC we saw sustained 5xx responses for a subset of requests (roughly 0.6% of traffic) that map to our payment flows. Our synthetic probes (attached) show retries and a TTL of errors starting ~02:17.

Your maintenance notice listed 02:00-02:30 UTC as the window; we expected normal behavior for most of that window but the error pattern looks like a partial degradation (not a clean maintenance cutover). Can you confirm whether the event is fully excluded under the maintenance exclusion terms or whether this should be considered partial degradation eligible for credit?

Attaching a short probe dump and a few sample error traces. We need a ledger-level explanation we can present to our procurement team by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Head of Integrations, ClarionHealth
elena@clarionhealth.com

Attachments:
- clarion_error_snippet_20271019.log (text)
- clarion_probe_sample_20271019.jsonl (jsonl)
From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Elena Rossi <elena@clarionhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-19T19:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Production errors during maintenance — ledger mismatch

Hi Elena — thanks for the details and the attachments. Looping in Marissa (SRE) and Lauren (AM) to coordinate a quick attribution. Initial notes: our maintenance window was 02:00–02:30 UTC but the planned activity was a rolling config push with no expected customer-facing disruption. We do see a short internal restart at ~02:05 for a control plane daemon (scheduled), but that should not have generated 5xx responses at 02:17.

Marissa — can you pull our probe telemetry and any vendor peering logs for 02:00–02:30 UTC and share a short breakdown on whether this looks like an internal partial-degrade or an external peering failover? If there is third-party attribution we should reference the clause in Section 3.2 of the SLA about vendor-chain exclusions.

Elena — we aim to get an initial technical summary + suggested ledger adjustment before EOD tomorrow.

Sergio Alvarez

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, Elena Rossi <elena@clarionhealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ops+status@acme-cloud.com
Date: 2027-10-19T23:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Production errors during maintenance — ledger mismatch

Thanks for the ping — I pulled the traces and correlated probe telemetry. Short version: there were two distinct things in the 02:00–02:30 window.

1) Scheduled control-plane restart: 02:05–02:07 UTC. No customer-facing 5xx spikes correlated to that; internal healthchecks recovered immediately.

2) Partial customer-facing degradation: 02:16–02:20 UTC we see elevated 5xx rates originating from one egress POP. Our egress telemetry shows an abrupt increase in TCP resets at 02:16:30 that align with a peering flap from a third-party CDN provider (OrionCDN). Orion's status page (linked below) lists a routing flap at 02:15–02:18 UTC in the us-east region. We received an ops postmortem excerpt from Orion (attached vendor_orion_postmortem_excerpt.pdf) confirming packet loss on their peering fabric.

Probe coverage note: Clara (our synthetic probe set) does not fully cover the path Clarion uses for payment flows; attached redwood_probe_coverage_20271019.csv shows limited fanout to Clarion's nearest gateway which means our ledger could undercount the user-visible impact. Clarion's synthetic probes captured the retry behavior because they originate from a different AS.

SLA interpretation: per Section 3.2, we exclude "third-party network provider failures" where the failure can be attributed to the provider and not to our routing or capacity. However, partial degradations where our service is a contributing factor remain eligible for credit. Given the telemetry, my current read is: primary cause = OrionCDN peering flap (third-party); contributing factor = transient routing fallback in one of our edge POPs that increased latency and retries for ~90s. That implies a split attribution.

Recommendation: propose a split credit calculation for the 02:16–02:20 window where Clarion's ledger shows errors. We will: 1) provide a per-minute token/availability ledger of the impacted minutes, 2) propose a percentage split reflecting ~70% third-party and ~30% Redwood responsibility based on request fail ratios and retry amplification seen in our traces. If Clarion prefers, we can escalate to full credit pending vendor confirmation, but that will require obtaining a formal acceptance from Orion and may take longer.

Attachments:
- redwood_probe_coverage_20271019.csv
- vendor_orion_postmortem_excerpt.pdf

Marissa Cole
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Production errors during maintenance — ledger mismatch

Thanks for the swift analysis and the transparency. Two items from Clarion's side:

- Procurement needs a dollar-equivalent for the credit. Please provide the per-minute impacted tokens and your proposed split (70/30 as a percentage) so we can map that to the fee schedule in our contract.
- We also want a short MAAP (mutual action and mitigation plan) for how Redwood will reduce impact risk going forward — specifically: improved probe fanout for our payment egress, and a runbook change for edge routing fallback behavior during peering flaps.

If you can send a draft ledger + credit amount and the MAAP doc (even as a shared Drive link) by tomorrow 17:00 UTC, procurement will review and we can close the loop. If vendor confirmation from Orion will delay that timeline, please flag and we'll accept a provisional split subject to change.

Appreciate the quick coordination.

Best,
Elena
